# Rule Maintenance

The conventions that govern the convention files themselves. Read this before editing anything under `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope

Applies to the agent-facing documentation of this repository.

Does **not** apply to human-facing docs — `README.md`, ADRs, runbooks. Those have readers with judgement; these have readers that follow instructions literally.

## Ownership

| Path                        | Owner    | Editing it means                                                             |
| --------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.claude/rules/agentkit/**` | agentkit | Your edit is overwritten by the next `agentkit sync`. Change the kit instead. |
| `.claude/rules/local/**`    | this repo | Free to edit. Never touched by sync.                                          |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`    | shared   | Only the span between `<!-- agentkit:start -->` and `<!-- agentkit:end -->` is generated. Everything outside it is the project's own. |
| `.agentkit/config.json`     | this repo | Which rules this project gets, and the values their placeholders need.        |
| `.agentkit/manifest.json`   | agentkit | Generated. Records what sync wrote, so it can detect a hand edit.              |

When a rule needs to change, the question is which of two things is true:

- **It is wrong or incomplete everywhere** → fix it in the agentkit repo, bump the kit, re-sync. Every project gets the fix.
- **It is only true here** → write it in `.claude/rules/local/`, or `agentkit eject` the rule and own the copy.

Copying a generated rule into `local/` and editing both is the one option that is never right — two files now claim the same authority and they will disagree.

## House style

Every rule file has the same shape, because an agent reading an unfamiliar rule should not also have to work out its structure:

1. `# Title`
2. One or two lines: **what goes wrong without this rule**, then what it ensures — linking the rule it builds on. State the problem first; a rule whose cost is visible and whose reason is not gets dropped the first time it is inconvenient.
3. `## Scope` — **Applies to**, then **Does not apply to**. Being explicit about the exclusions is what stops a rule being applied where it is wrong.
4. Topic sections, each: principle → `CORRECT` / `WRONG` snippet or table → rationale → exceptions.
5. `## NEVER Do` — the rule's content restated as a flat, checkable list.

Write rules as instructions to an agent, not as observations about the codebase: `Prefer X over Y`, `Never Z`. A rule that describes rather than directs gets read as background and ignored.

## Changes land together

> When a rename lands, it lands in code, rules, `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` and the skills that cite the old name — in the same commit.

A rule that names something no longer in the codebase is worse than no rule: it is confidently wrong, and an agent has no way to tell. The same applies in reverse — a convention introduced in code without a rule will be undone by the next agent that touches the file.

## Keep rules small and linked

One concept per file. When two rules overlap, generalize them into one principle and fold the specific cases in as examples — prefer one abstract rule over two concrete ones.

A file that has grown several unrelated topics is no longer one concept. Split it: a reader looking for the logging format should not have to walk past nested-data access to find it, and a one-line pointer in `AGENTS.md` cannot honestly summarize seven subjects at once.

If no existing file's title and Scope cover the rule you are adding, propose a new file and ask before creating it.

The goal is a distilled, highly curated expression of a personal style that stays project-agnostic, so it can be carried into any codebase and reused as-is. A rule that only makes sense in one repository belongs in that repository's `.claude/rules/local/`.

Cross-link rather than repeat. A core rule links only to other core rules; a profile rule may link to core. Never link from core to a profile — the profile may not be installed in the project reading the link.

## NEVER Do

- Edit a file under `.claude/rules/agentkit/` — the next sync discards it.
- Keep a hand-edited copy of a generated rule alongside the generated one.
- Write a rule as an observation instead of an instruction.
- Add a rule without a `## Scope` section saying where it does **not** apply.
- Rename something in code without updating every rule, doc and skill that cites the old name in the same change.
- Link from a core rule to a profile rule.
- Put project-specific vocabulary, paths or exception lists into a kit rule — that is what `.claude/rules/local/` is for.
